criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.

stories.notes: The synced plan.json has no requirements, guardrails, systems or measures, an empty project name, and placeholder dates (every release and due date on 2026-09-20). The page renders those as empty states rather than filling them in.

criteria.text: Given the system is ready for deployment, when the deployment process is initiated, then the system should be operational with core functionalities.
Given the system is deployed, when a core functionality is accessed, then it should perform as expected.
Trust: Given the deployment process, when it completes, then an audit log entry is created with deployment details.

stories.notes: Deploy with `npm run deploy` (on-premises, this machine). It opens the database, listens, checks /api/health and the asset records over HTTP with timeouts and capped retries, then writes a system.deploy audit event (version, commit, host, database, checks, duration); the deployment does not count until that event is written. Failures (port taken, health unreachable, database will not open, audit write fails) stop the server and are audited as system.deploy_failed where the database allows. Core functionalities agreed with the user: health check plus asset records (create/read, audited, idempotent by asset tag). Not done here: Active Directory sign-in and 2FA (REQ-010) — sign-in is still a development stand-in until STORY-012; near-real-time replication (REQ-002 option) is not built.

criteria.text: Given the system is connected to ESRI ArcGIS, when asset data is updated, then GIS layers should reflect these updates.
Given a GIS field value is changed, when I check the system, then it should show the updated value.
Trust: Ensure all GIS transactions are logged for audit.

stories.notes: Verified against a SIMULATED ArcGIS stand-in (tools/arcgis-standin, layer named 'SIMULATED · City Assets') that speaks the ESRI REST shapes the client uses: generateToken, layer metadata with editor tracking, query with paging, applyEdits, errors as HTTP 200 with codes 498/499. Not yet run against the City's real ArcGIS Enterprise 11.3: point ARCGIS_LAYER_URL / ARCGIS_TOKEN_URL / ARCGIS_USERNAME / ARCGIS_PASSWORD at it and run npm run gis-sync. Field ownership agreed with the user: the system owns ASSET_TAG, NAME, ASSET_TYPE, STATUS, LOCATION_DESC (pushed); GIS owns geometry and all other attributes (pulled, shown on the asset). A GIS edit to a system-owned field is audited as gis.mismatch and overwritten by the system value. Every GIS transaction is audited: gis.push, gis.push_failed, gis.pull, gis.mismatch, gis.sync_run, gis.sync_failed. Failure paths: auth (bad sign-in, rejected token, one refresh on expiry), latency (timeouts, capped retries; applyEdits never retried, adds look up the tag first so nothing duplicates), data mismatch (owned-field edits, unknown features, missing layer fields).

criteria.text: Given an asset is added to the system, when I view its details, then I should see its lifecycle status.
Given an asset's condition changes, when I update its status, then the system should reflect the new condition.
Trust: Ensure all asset updates are logged for audit.

stories.notes: Inventory (filter, search, paging), lifecycle (allowed moves only; retired is final), condition readings (good, fair, poor, critical; append-only; current = latest by observed time) and one-off maintenance tasks with due dates and overdue flags. Dashboard at /assets. Every change and refusal is audited. Failure paths: data entry errors name each wrong field; illegal or out-of-date status updates are refused and audited, and a refused move also discards its reading; condition discrepancies (critical but active, late older reading, two readings for one moment, retired with open work) are flagged and audited, and the status is left for a person to change. Criteria proven by HTTP tests and a real deployment. Not proven: the /assets page was served and its script syntax-checked, but it has not been clicked through in a browser. REQ-001 is not finished by this story: no load test for about 80 users, no recurring maintenance, no real sign-in (STORY-012), and Cityworks data is not migrated (STORY-013). The status moves and the condition scale were chosen during the build and need confirming with the City's asset managers. Condition and maintenance are not sent to GIS.

criteria.text: Given asset data is updated, when I check GIS, then the spatial information should be accurate.
Given a synchronization error occurs, when I review logs, then I should see error details.
Trust: Ensure synchronization logs are maintained for audit.

stories.notes: Verified against the SIMULATED ArcGIS stand-in, not yet against the City's ArcGIS Enterprise 11.3, so the 'accurate' in criterion 1 means accurate as read back from the stand-in. Pushed features are read back and compared (gis.verify_failed if the layer holds something else). Geometry stays owned by GIS, so spatial problems are flagged, never corrected: changed location text opens a location_review until the point moves, and an invalid or out-of-area point never replaces a good one. A whole-layer comparison runs at least daily (or --reconcile) and finds deleted features, which are not recreated, and edits that skipped editor tracking. Duplicate features cannot take over a link. A run lock stops two jobs racing. Every stopped run is audited as gis.sync_failed with stage, asset, error and a next step, including unexpected errors. Review with npm run gis-log (-- --errors), GET /api/gis/log and GET /api/gis/status. Logs live in the append-only audit trail. Limits: the out-of-area check needs the layer to publish an extent and only applies to point layers; a bad point replaces an open location_review flag, so that flag can be lost if GIS then returns to the same point; the audit trail has no retention or archiving policy, and gis.sync_run adds a row every run; ESRI code 1019 for a missing feature is from memory and needs checking against real 11.3, though the whole-layer comparison finds deletions regardless.

criteria.text: Given a user attempts to log in, when the credentials are correct, then access should be granted with enhanced security protocols.
Given a user attempts to log in, when the credentials are incorrect, then access should be denied and an alert should be logged.
Trust: All login attempts must be recorded with IP address and timestamp for security auditing.

stories.notes: Real sign-in replaces the development role picker: password (salted scrypt), then a required TOTP code (RFC 6238, checked against its published vector), then a session in an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie. Role headers now work only when a test asks createApp for them; nothing that starts the real system can enable them. Failure paths: incorrect password (same answer whether or not the user exists; alert logged); wrong, reused or moved code; brute force (limits per user and address, per user, per address, including parallel bursts; alert logged once); session hijack (other IP or browser ends the session); expired session (30 minutes idle, 8 hours maximum). Every attempt is audited with IP and time before the answer goes out, and if it cannot be written the login is refused. REQ-010 is NOT met by this story: accounts are local, with no Active Directory and no single sign-on, because this project cannot reach a directory. docs/SECURITY.md documents PII handling, and retention is left as a City decision. Not proven: no page has been clicked through in a browser, including the new login page and the three pages changed to use it. API flows were tested over HTTP and pages only confirmed as served. Not built: changing your own password, password reset, self-service authenticator setup, QR codes, TLS in the server itself (deploy refuses to listen beyond this machine without a TLS proxy). Not penetration tested.
